title: Box office seat holds with a 10-minute window
scenario: Replay a two-day on-sale log of hold/confirm/release events against a seat map. Holds last 10 minutes (inclusive) and confirms need an active hold by the same customer.

verified.why_correct: Sorting on (at, seq) looks like it could be just `at`, but seq is the file position, so events with the same timestamp (E01/E02) keep file order, as rule 1 requires. `at` is a parsed datetime, so the mixed formats sort correctly.

bugs.title: Customer ids only trimmed, not upper-cased
bugs.symptom: Test 1: B1, B3 and A6 are missing from sold, and C03/C05 are missing from by_customer (C02 only has A2). Test 2: no_hold is 6 instead of 3, revenue 436.0 instead of 627.0, occupancy 35.0 instead of 50.0.
bugs.why: Holds written as `c03`/` c05`/`c02` and confirms written as `C03`/`C05`/`C02` no longer belong to the same customer, so each of those confirms fails the holder check and is rejected as no_hold.
bugs.unblocks: B1, B3 and A6 in the sold map, C02/C03/C05 in by_customer, and the Test 2 numbers. Exposes B2.
hints: B1, B3 and A6 were never sold. Find their hold and confirm rows in events.csv and compare them.
Look at how customer ids are cleaned in the loader, compared with seat ids.
probes: Why did the seat ids not have the same problem?
Why did fixing this make a different seat (B3) stop selling?

bugs.title: Hold window made exclusive
bugs.old: return hold is not None and age_seconds(hold.held_at, now) <= HOLD_SECONDS
bugs.new: return hold is not None and age_seconds(hold.held_at, now) < HOLD_SECONDS
bugs.symptom: Only visible after B1 is fixed. Test 1: B3 is not sold and C05 is missing from by_customer. Test 2: no_hold 4, revenue 571.5, occupancy 45.0.
bugs.why: C05's confirm (E10) comes exactly 10:00 after the hold (E09). The spec says that is still in time, but `<` treats the hold as already expired.
bugs.unblocks: B3 in the sold map, C05 in by_customer, and the Test 2 numbers.
hints: How long after E09 does E10 happen?
probes: Why was this hidden while customer ids weren't upper-cased?
Which other events go through is_active, and why didn't they change?

bugs.title: Hold age ignores whole days
bugs.symptom: Test 1: C2 is sold to C10 instead of C11. Test 2: seat_held is 2 instead of 1 (no_hold stays 3: C11's confirm is rejected and C10's goes through). Revenue and occupancy are unchanged.
bugs.why: `timedelta.seconds` is only the seconds part after whole days are removed. C10's hold from day 1 looks 2 minutes old on day 2, so it blocks C11's hold and then lets C10 confirm.
bugs.unblocks: C2 in the sold map and by_customer, and the seat_held/no_hold counts.
hints: C2 went to C10, whose hold was placed the day before. How old was that hold at E21?
Look at how the age of a hold is computed.
probes: Why do the other holds work fine with .seconds?

context_qa.a: It creates a `BoxOffice` with the seat map, sorts the events with `sort_events`, and calls `office.apply(event)` for each one. `apply` dispatches on the action string to the `hold`, `confirm` or `release` method.

context_qa.q: Where is a hold's age computed, and in what unit?
context_qa.a: `booking.is_active` calls `utils.age_seconds(hold.held_at, now)` and compares the result with `HOLD_SECONDS`, which is 600.

context_qa.q: What does BoxOffice keep track of?
context_qa.a: `holds` (seat id → Hold with customer and held_at), `sold` (seat id → customer id) and `rejections` (a Counter of reason strings).

context_qa.q: How are ids cleaned when the CSVs are loaded?
context_qa.a: `load_seats` runs `norm_id` on seat ids. `load_events` builds each Event with `norm_id` for the seat and its own cleaning for the customer, and lower-cases the action.

context_qa.q: When does confirm() reject an event?
context_qa.a: When the seat is already in `sold`, when there is no active hold on the seat, or when the hold belongs to a different customer id. All three are counted as `no_hold`.

context_qa.q: How are revenue and occupancy computed?
context_qa.a: In `build_report`: revenue sums `seats[s].price` over sold seats and rounds to 2 decimals; occupancy is `100 * len(sold) / len(seats)` rounded to 1 decimal.
